title: Travel Time Estimator: Drive Time and Distance
description: Estimate typical driving time and road distance between places with the Travel Time Estimator — network estimates for trip planning. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, a pair the map shows 190 miles apart returns roughly three and a quarter hours of typical driving — the estimate a plan, not a promise, is built from.
quick_answer: The Travel Time Estimator returns the typical driving duration and road distance between an origin and a destination, computed over the road network. Set the two places and read the figures trip plans are sketched from — honest network estimates, openly not live traffic and not a guarantee.

“Can we visit both in a day?” is two estimates and an addition. Answer it at the desk.
Typical times make routes comparable in a way live times cannot — today's jam is not the route's character.
Before quoting a window to anyone, the typical estimate is the floor the promise must respect.

The estimator says 3 h 15 min for a pair; the navigation app says 4 h 05 min at 8 a.m. Both are right: one describes the road, the other describes this morning. Planning uses the first; departing uses the second.
The estimator works wherever the open road data reaches — which is most of the mapped world, with quality that follows the mappers.

popular_table.intro: Two kinds of truth about the same pair of places — use each for its own job.
popular_table.note: The estimator's distance is the stable half of its answer; treat its duration as typical, and your departure margin as wisdom.

faq: No — by design. It reports typical durations from the road network's speeds, the right basis for planning. Live conditions are a navigation app's layer at departure time.
Wherever open road data covers — most of the world, with rural and newly built areas thinner in places. The estimate is only as good as the map beneath it.
Why is road distance longer than straight-line?
The estimator routes on roads, so its distance is the driven one — longer than the crow's, shorter than your detours.
Can route results change over time?
Slightly, as the open data improves: new roads shorten some pairs forever. Re-run standing plans each season.
How is this different from the ETA Calculator?
This page returns the network's typical time for a pair; the ETA Calculator divides your distance by your average speed and adds it to a departure. Sketch here, commit there.
Which end of a range should I plan on?
The estimate is a single typical figure, not a range — add your own margin for the hour and season you will travel.
This estimator is the road-driving one; the site's other planners cover walking and cycling networks with the same honesty.
